12. Post the approved disposition on the same day wherever the shift allows: release restock to its system-directed location, transfer rework to its holding position, and remove scrapped units through the authorised scrap route.
13. Retain the quarantine record, assessment, approval and system adjustment together for audit, linking the stock adjustment to the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment that authorised it.
14. Review open quarantine positions at each shift handover, carrying unresolved assessments forward with named owner and required completion time until closure.

title: Value-added packing
text:
1. Complete all rework, kitting and labelling in Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
2. Inspect returns in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling before releasing any unit to value-added work.
3. Direct returns staff to inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each unit.
4. Obtain prior shift-supervisor approval of the disposition before executing any restock, rework or scrap of inspected returns.
5. Transfer approved rework units to the designated rework holding position inside Zone F immediately after approval.
6. Carry out packing rework in Zone F only against a system task or supervisor instruction.
7. Carry out labelling in Zone F using scan-verified labels matched to the system receipt or outbound order.
8. Carry out kitting in Zone F from scan-verified components and confirm each finished kit in the system.
9. Apply PR-05 Packing and labelling requirements to every value-added pack, including label confirmation and system recording.
10. Segregate any component found damaged during rework and assess it under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling before further use.
11. Return excess components and unused packaging to their system-directed locations and never stage them in picking aisles.
12. Remove picking waste such as stretch film, strapping and empty cartons to waste cages throughout the shift.
13. Feed clean cardboard to the site cardboard baler; the site has 1 cardboard baler.
14. Operate that baler through a full compression cycle and tie off each baler bale before ejection.
15. Store finished bales clear of wrapper lanes, staging lanes and dock approaches until collection.
16. Keep rework benches, kitting tables and labelling stations clear of waste, tools and unassigned stock at end of work.

title: Cold-chain handling
text:
1. Execute all chilled storage, movement and monitoring under PR-12 Cold-chain handling without deviation from this section.

2. Treat Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C for all product requiring controlled refrigeration.

3. Hold the cold zone at or above +2 °C at every location, at every level, during all operating hours and overnight.

4. Hold the cold zone at or below +8 °C at every location, at every level, including during put-away, picking, replenishment and stock counting activity.

5. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift with the calibrated monitoring equipment provided for Zone E.

6. Record each shift verification in the designated temperature log immediately after reading, noting time and result against the +2 to +8 °C range.

7. Keep doors and curtains closed except for active pallet movements, and minimise dwell time inside Zone E to protect the +2 to +8 °C envelope.

8. Transfer chilled pallets directly between inbound inspection and Zone E without intermediate staging in ambient areas.

9. Move outbound chilled pallets directly from Zone E to the dispatch staging area and prioritise prompt loading onto the waiting vehicle.

10. Place incoming batches behind existing stock in Zone E and select the earliest expiry first unless the system directs otherwise.

11. Isolate any pallet found outside the permitted temperature range at once and move it to quarantine in Zone F for assessment.

12. Prevent release of temperature-affected stock to picking or return to Zone E until authorised assessment is complete and documented.

13. Restrict Zone E entry to personnel engaged in put-away, replenishment, picking, stock counting or supervision of those tasks.

14. Brief forklift operators and pickers assigned to Zone E on PR-12 Cold-chain handling before they commence chilled work.

15. Instruct the shift supervisor to review each shift temperature record, investigate any deviation from +2 °C or +8 °C, and escalate loss of control immediately.

16. Maintain backup monitoring devices available at the charging station area and replace any suspect sensor without delaying the next each shift verification.

17. Suspend routine replenishment and picking in Zone E while temperature recovery is in progress following a verified excursion.

18. Confirm restoration of the +2 to +8 °C condition through successive stable readings before resuming normal chilled operations under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

title: Hazmat handling
text:
1. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, storage, movement and spill involving hazardous materials without exception.
2. Store all hazmat only inside the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
3. Treat the hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 as a segregated controlled store and keep its boundaries, signage and access clear at all times.
4. Enforce the cage stock ceiling strictly during put-away, replenishment and returns transfer.
5. Verify that no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time before authorising any additional pallet movement inward.
6. Calculate the running cage total from system stock plus staged inbound pallets before transporting any further pallet to the cage.
7. Retain a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg as the planning figure for every hazmat pallet weight assessment.
8. Plan cage occupancy on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight).
9. Reject any inbound or transferred pallet that would lift the cage above 4,000 kg and hold the excess pallet in the system-directed holding location pending release or onward instruction.
10. Check packaging integrity, labelling, compatibility and stability of each pallet before placement inside the 60 m2 cage.
11. Position compatible products together inside the cage and separate incompatible classes in accordance with the product safety data sheet.
12. Secure each pallet against movement, maintain clear access for inspection and emergency intervention, and never block cage doors or spill equipment.
13. Inspect the cage for leaks, damaged packaging, missing labels and blocked access before adding stock and after completing any handling task.
14. Initiate spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response immediately on discovering any leak, drip, damaged container or vapour release.
15. Stop all handling work in the affected area, warn personnel nearby, and prevent unauthorised entry to the spill zone.
16. Contain the spread using the designated spill materials where safe to do so and avoid allowing liquid to enter drains, aisles or adjacent storage.
17. Ventilate the area where instructed by the product safety data sheet and remove ignition sources where flammability is indicated.
18. Decontaminate affected packaging, equipment and floor surfaces only with approved materials and dispose of contaminated absorbents through the approved waste route.
19. Record the product identity, quantity involved, cage weight position, cause, containment actions and final disposition in the system promptly after the event.
20. Reconcile the cage running total after any loss, disposal or transfer out and confirm that no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat remains stored before resuming normal receipts.

title: Emergency evacuation
text:
Execute PR-14 Emergency evacuation immediately on alarm, discovered fire, confirmed gas leak, structural damage or direct instruction from supervision.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

1. Activate the nearest fire alarm call point when discovering fire, smoke, gas odour or flooding.
2. Alert surrounding personnel verbally while moving toward the nearest safe exit.
3. Stop all handling work at once and make equipment safe only where seconds allow.
4. Lower forks fully, apply the parking brake and switch off the truck before leaving it.
5. Close open dock doors on the escape route where operation remains possible without delay.
6. Leave racking aisles by the marked cross-aisles, never by passing under raised loads.
7. Follow green running-man signage and segregated routes toward the designated assembly point.
8. Assist visitors and contractors encountered on the route and direct them to exit with you.
9. Report to the assembly point without diverting to locker areas, offices or the yard parking.
10. Assemble by shift group at the assembly point and remain clear of access roads for emergency vehicles.
11. Report missing persons, last known location and nature of the emergency to the shift supervisor.
12. Prohibit smoking, telephone distraction and departure from the assembly area until released.

Control re-entry centrally under supervision. Roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.

13. Conduct roll call from roster and visitor log using names, not headcounts alone.
14. Repeat the roll call after late arrivals join and after stragglers are confirmed.
15. Forbid re-entry for personal items, trucks or staged pallets until authorisation is given.
16. Authorise re-entry only after the all-clear and confirmed safe condition of the building.
17. Re-enter in supervised groups through announced entrances when released to do so.
18. Resume work only on instruction and report residual hazards, damage or blocked routes at once.

Maintain readiness through regular practice. An evacuation drill runs every quarter.

19. Attend every scheduled drill as rostered and treat each drill as a live evacuation.
20. Test alternative escape routes during drills so all shifts practise primary and secondary exits.
21. Record drill date, evacuation time, attendance and deficiencies in the drill log.
22. Debrief deficiencies immediately after the drill and assign corrective actions with owners.
23. Complete incident reports for every real evacuation, alarm activation and drill failure.
24. Submit each report promptly for review without waiting for the next shift.
25. Ensure the shift supervisor reviews every incident report.
26. Implement agreed corrections to signage, routes, lighting or briefing before the next working day.
27. Brief absent staff on return on any route change arising from a drill or incident.
28. Keep assembly-point lists, contact numbers and visitor logs current and available at the muster location.

title: Operator Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. Operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks only when authorised as a forklift operator under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
2. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
3. Accountability of the warehouse manager covers the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including MHE authorisations.

4. Know your fleet before starting work:
(a) 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t;
(b) 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t;
(c) 8 electric pallet jacks;
(d) 12 hand pallet jacks.
Select the truck type rated for the load. Never exceed a pallet gross weight of 800 kg, including its load.

5. Complete the documented pre-use check every day before first use of each forklift.
6. Carry out the same documented pre-use check each day before first use of each reach truck and each electric pallet jack.
7. Record each daily check in the designated log before moving the truck.
8. Isolate any truck with overdue planned maintenance, failed brakes, defective steering, damaged forks, faulty lights, leaking hydraulics or unreadable capacity plate.
9. Park defective MHE in the designated quarantine line and attach a do-not-use tag.
10. Notify the maintenance technician immediately about every defect found during checks or operation.
11. Understand that the maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
12. Wait for release by the maintenance technician before returning a quarantined truck to use.
13. Fasten your seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
14. Adjust mirrors, seat and steering position while stationary with the parking brake applied.
15. Test controls at low speed in a clear area after completing the daily check.
16. Report missing or illegible daily check sheets before starting operation.
17. Surrender authorisation documents on request during supervision checks.
18. Attend refresher briefing when instructed following any incident or observed unsafe act.
19. Comply with all further driving, speed and pedestrian rules in PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation before continuing duties on the floor.

title: Speed Limits and Driving Rules
text:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation on every truck movement inside the building and in the outdoor yard.
2. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse wherever trucks and pedestrians share the same area.
3. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building under any load condition.
4. Reduce speed further to match visibility, congestion and floor conditions, even where 8 km/h would otherwise be permitted.
5. Drive main transport aisles with heightened caution, recognising they are 4.0 m wide and carry two-way truck and pedestrian crossing traffic.
6. Enter rack storage aisles at a controlled speed, recognising they are 3.0 m wide with limited clearance for turning and passing.
7. Give way to pedestrians and trucks already established in narrow aisles before proceeding.
8. Slow to 5 km/h before every marked pedestrian zone and crossing, and maintain that limit until the truck has fully cleared the markings.
9. Stop and yield where pedestrians are present on or approaching a crossing, regardless of priority.
10. Respect segregated pedestrian walkways at all times, recognising they are 1.2 m wide and are not to be entered, blocked or used for staging.
11. Sound the horn at blind corners, aisle intersections and dock approaches where sight lines are restricted.
12. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving, and confirm it is latched before setting off.
13. Keep forks low during travel, load stable and tilted back, and mast clear of racking, doors and pedestrians.
14. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, and slow earlier for turns, gradients, wet surfaces and parked vehicles.
15. Approach dock doors 1-4 serving inbound receiving only when directed, and park squarely before loading or unloading.
16. Approach dock doors 5-8 serving outbound dispatch only when directed, and wait clear of the leveller approach until authorised to advance.
17. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches, and proceed straight on and off the leveller without turning.
18. Keep a safe distance from the dock edge, a docked vehicle and other trucks queuing at adjacent doors.
19. Stop the truck and report unsafe speed, congestion, blocked walkways or obscured markings through the site reporting route.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Conduct
text:
1. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every movement on foot across the warehouse floor. Treat segregated routes, crossings and truck areas as binding controls, not guidance.

2. Stay inside the segregated pedestrian walkways whenever you move between zones. The segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from truck traffic.

3. Keep the full width of the walkway clear. Never place pallets, waste, handling equipment or work materials in the walkway, on its markings or across its entrances.

4. Wear a high-visibility vest for every entry to the warehouse floor, without exception. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.

5. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor at all times. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

6. Use only marked pedestrian zones and crossings to cross traffic routes. Stop at the edge, look both ways, establish eye contact with approaching drivers and cross only when trucks have stopped.

7. Expect forklifts to pass at up to 8 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

8. Expect reduced truck speed where you walk. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Do not step out until the truck has completed its slowdown and the driver has acknowledged you.

9. Keep clear of the main transport aisles except at marked crossings. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and carry two-way truck traffic.

10. Do not walk down rack storage aisles unless your task requires it. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide and leave limited clearance beside operating trucks. Face oncoming trucks, keep to the rack line and never walk between a moving truck and the racking.

11. Keep clear of dock ramps and leveller approaches. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches, but pedestrians must not use ramps as walkways or shortcuts.

12. Observe dock separation. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Do not enter staging or door approaches unless your task requires it.

13. Enter a dock door area only for an assigned load. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Follow the door assignment and the marked pedestrian route to the door.

14. Never walk behind a reversing truck, between a truck and a dock edge, or under a raised leveller lip or raised forks. Make yourself visible and wait in the marked waiting position until loading or unloading movements stop.

15. Report faded lines, damaged barriers, blocked crossings or obscured signage to the shift supervisor immediately. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

16. Stop work and warn others if you see a pedestrian outside a walkway, a blocked walkway forcing pedestrians into traffic, or a truck failing to slow at a crossing. Correct the route before continuing work.

title: Mandatory PPE
text:
1. Wear a compliant high-visibility vest whenever present on the warehouse floor.
High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, without exception for role, task duration or escorted status.
Keep each vest fully fastened and uncovered by coats, totes or harnesses so conspicuity remains continuous.

2. Obtain a replacement vest immediately when soiling, fading, tearing or reflector damage reduces visibility.
Spare compliant vests and footwear are held at the charging station area for immediate exchange.
Discard unserviceable vests through the designated waste route and never retain them for further use.

3. Put on safety footwear class S3 before stepping beyond the floor entry point.
Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor for all personnel, contractors and escorted visitors.
Inspect footwear regularly for split uppers, exposed toe caps, worn tread or failed fastenings.

4. Change out of damaged or non-compliant footwear without delay and report the shortfall to supervision.
Wearing trainers, wellingtons, low-grade safety shoes or any other substitute remains prohibited anywhere on the floor.
Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse for briefing, walkway use and crossing discipline alongside PPE compliance.

5. Fasten the seat belt before moving any counterbalance forklift, reach truck or other ride-on truck.
Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and yard travel.
Adjust belt tension to remove slack while retaining full reach to steering, hydraulics and mirrors.

6. Leave the belt fastened until the truck has stopped completely with parking brake applied.
Never defeat interlocks, tuck buckles behind seats or operate with an unlatched belt for convenience.
Follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for authorisation, daily checks, speed limits and operating conduct.

7. Report any cut, frayed, jammed or non-latching seat belt to the maintenance technician before further operation.
Quarantine the affected truck in the designated quarantine line until repair and release are confirmed.
Notify supervision promptly where missing, incorrect or damaged PPE prevents safe task commencement.

8. Accept that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
Compliance with hi-vis, S3 footwear and seat-belt requirements forms part of that site-wide safety accountability.
Enforce these mandates on every shift, challenge non-compliance directly and record repeat failures for review.

9. Brief visitors and new starters on these PPE mandates before floor entry under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
Confirm each entrant wears a fastened vest and S3 footwear before escorting beyond the entry point.
Deny access to any person unable to meet the standard until suitable PPE is provided.

10. Integrate PPE checks into PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation daily routines and pedestrian supervision.
During pre-use checks verify personal vest, footwear and belt condition alongside truck roadworthiness.
Sustain consistent enforcement so protection remains effective across receiving, storage, picking and dispatch operations.

title: Cold Zone Rules
text:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to all work in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Do not use Zone E for ambient storage, staging, or general waiting.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C. Treat any reading outside +2 to +8 °C as a temperature excursion. Stop further put-away and picking for the affected stock and notify the shift supervisor at once.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Ensure the verification is completed, recorded, and reviewed on every shift:

4. Complete the Shift 1 verification during Shift 1. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Record the reading, the measuring device identity, and the time of check. Report any deviation before continuing routine chilled work.

5. Complete the Shift 2 verification during Shift 2. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Record the reading, the measuring device identity, and the time of check. Hand over any unresolved excursion, door fault, or monitoring fault to the next responsible person with the record attached.

6. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment in Zone E at all times. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Add approved thermal clothing for extended cold exposure and change out of damp clothing without delay.

7. Limit time in Zone E to the task in hand. Plan replenishment, picking, and counting tasks before entry to reduce door-open time. Close cold-zone doors immediately after each pallet or personnel movement and never wedge them open.

8. Move chilled pallets without delay between controlled areas and Zone E. Do not stage chilled goods in ambient aisles, dispatch lanes, or dock approaches. Prioritise unloading, booking, and put-away of chilled inbound so exposure outside +2 to +8 °C is minimised.

9. Check packaging, labels, and pallet stability before handling chilled stock. Reject wet, collapsed, or leaking units for assessment under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Keep floors dry, report ice or condensation immediately, and walk at a controlled pace on cold surfaces.

10. Keep Zone E clear for safe movement and airflow. Do not block evaporators, sensors, aisles, or emergency exits with pallets or equipment. Park handling equipment outside the cold zone unless actively loading or unloading, and switch off idle trucks to limit heat and exhaust.

11. Respond to alarms, visible misting loss, warm product, or sensor failure as an incident. Secure the area, preserve the temperature record, and escalate to the shift supervisor. Do not release suspect stock for picking or dispatch until PR-12 Cold-chain handling authorises its disposition.

title: Site Layout and Dock Discipline
text:
1. Learn the site footprint before working unsupervised. The warehouse floor covers 6,000 m2 and the building has 8 dock doors. Memorise the zone letters, the door numbers and the direction of flow from receiving through to dispatch.

2. Enter Zone A only for assigned receiving work. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Keep its inspection lanes clear for inbound operators and give way to unloading trucks.

3. Respect the storage and picking areas. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Within both zones follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for truck movements and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse for walking routes.

4. Stage outbound freight only where directed. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Never obstruct staging lanes, wrapper lanes or dock approaches with pallets, waste or equipment.

5. Treat temperature-controlled and service areas as restricted. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Enter Zone E or work in Zone F only when your task requires it and close cold-zone doors immediately after each movement.

6. Use the correct dock doors for each movement. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Drive to the allocated door only and never cross between inbound and outbound aprons without instruction.

7. Obtain door and slot confirmation before positioning. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Wait for your door assignment, confirm the time slot and follow banksman signals during reversing and docking.

8. Control speed on every yard and dock movement. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Reduce further in rain, poor light or congested conditions.

9. Maintain discipline around levellers, ramps and pedestrians. Stop before each leveller approach, check seating and edge guards and proceed at walking pace. Yield to pedestrians on marked crossings at all times under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

10. Report layout hazards immediately and secure the area. Notify supervision of blocked aisles, damaged barriers, faulty dock equipment or incorrectly parked trailers. Do not attempt to use an unsafe door, ramp or leveller until it is cleared and released.

title: Racking and Stacking Limits
text:
1. Apply PR-02 Put-away to storage for every pallet placed into bulk storage or block stack.
2. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
3. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions across the Zone B bays.
4. Verify the system-directed location before lifting any pallet to height.
5. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.
6. Reject overweight units at the put-away face and return them for reassessment.
7. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg in total across all beam levels.
8. Distribute heavy pallets to lower beam levels within that bay limit.
9. Never concentrate full-weight pallets on upper beams where the bay total would be exceeded.
10. Use reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for placement and retrieval in the high bays.
11. Use counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t only where the aisle and rack configuration permits safe access.
12. Stop put-away immediately if the scanner shows the bay already at its rated load.
13. Apply free block stacking only where racking locations are not available and the system explicitly directs it.
14. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
15. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
16. Apply both block-stack limits together; exceeding either limit prohibits further stacking.
17. Align stacked pallets squarely face to face with no overhang or lean.
18. Keep block stacks clear of main transport aisles, rack storage aisles, pedestrian walkways, dock approaches and emergency exits.
19. Never climb racking or stacked pallets to reposition stock or labels.
20. Report any observed upright damage, beam deformation, missing safety pins or anchor failure to the maintenance technician at once.
21. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
22. Do not reload a damaged or overloaded bay until the maintenance technician has cleared and released it.
23. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
24. Cooperate with the monthly inspection by clearing access and reporting defects found during PR-02 Put-away to storage.
25. Record beam impacts, scrapes or loose pallets found between inspections without delay.
26. In Zone B maintain safe separation between trucks and pedestrians during all put-away and retrieval movements.

title: Hazmat Storage Limits
text:
1. Store all hazardous materials only in the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
2. Do not store hazmat in any other zone, racking, staging lane, or general floor area.
3. Zone F holds the value-added services area, and the hazmat cage is the sole authorised location for hazmat within it.
4. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, movement, inspection, and storage of hazmat.
5. Keep the hazmat cage inside Zone F clear, locked, signed, and accessible for inspection at all times.
6. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2; do not extend storage beyond its marked walls, doors, and floor markings.
7. Hold no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time.
8. Verify the running cage weight total before transporting any additional pallet to the hazmat cage.
9. Refuse any delivery to the cage that would take the total above 4,000 kg and segregate the excess outside the cage.
10. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg; use this limit when calculating cage capacity.
11. The hazmat cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets; treat five pallets at maximum weight as a full cage.
12. Record every pallet weight on receipt and maintain a visible running total at the cage entrance.
13. Update the running total immediately after each placement and each removal.
14. Inspect labelling, packaging integrity, and segregation inside the cage on every handling.
15. Report leaks, damaged packaging, missing labels, and blocked access for immediate action under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Keep incompatible materials separated in line with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and label instructions.
17. Prohibit ignition sources, open flames, and unauthorised electrical equipment inside and immediately around the cage.
18. Allow entry only to trained personnel assigned to the hazmat task; exclude all other staff and visitors.
19. Wear the prescribed protective equipment for the material handled and ensure spill equipment is available before moving hazmat.
20. Transport hazmat pallets one at a time by the authorised route and place them directly into the designated cage position.
21. Do not stage hazmat pallets in aisles, dock areas, or Zone F work areas while awaiting cage space.
22. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including approval of any change to hazmat storage arrangements.
23. Obtain prior approval through the warehouse manager before accepting any new hazmat line or increased stock above planned levels.
24. Stop all further placements to the cage when the 4,000 kg limit or the 5 full-weight pallet limit is reached and escalate the overflow.
25. Never use general quarantine, bulk racking, or dispatch staging as overflow for hazmat.
26. Audit cage stock weight, pallet count, and documentation daily and correct any discrepancy before the next receipt.

title: Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods
text:
1. Stop work in the affected area immediately when you discover a leak, spill or damaged container. Warn nearby personnel, eliminate ignition sources where safe to do so, and prevent the substance spreading to aisles, drains or other zones.

2. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every chemical, fuel, battery-acid or unidentified liquid spill. Follow the spill-kit instructions for containment and absorption, wear the specified protective equipment, and ventilate the area as directed.

3. Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Do not attempt clean-up beyond your training; wait for instruction and handover control of the scene on arrival.

4. Segregate all suspect, leaking, temperature-affected or damaged stock at once. Move affected pallets and cartons to quarantine, using clean handling equipment to avoid cross-contamination.

5. Place all quarantined stock only in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not leave quarantined goods in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch aisles, on dock approaches or in pedestrian walkways.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep quarantine, inspection, rework and value-added tasks physically separated within Zone F. Maintain clear access to the quarantine area for inspection and removal at all times.

7. Returns are inspected in Zone F. Transfer inbound returns directly to the inspection point and hold them there until disposition is decided. Do not restock, rework or scrap any return before inspection is complete.

8. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the inspection result, quantity, condition and proposed disposition in the system and attach the disposition label to each unit.

9. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every damaged, crushed, punctured, wet or contaminated unit found on receipt, in storage, during picking or on return. Photograph the damage, retain packaging and labels where safe, and enter the full quantity and value in the damage record.

10. Obtain write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any damaged stock. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

11. Apply the approval threshold to each damage event separately. Do not divide one event to remain within a lower limit. Escalate any dispute over value or responsibility to the shift supervisor for decision.

12. Release quarantined stock only on written authorisation in the system. Return cleared goods to their directed location, send approved rework to the designated position, and dispatch scrap through the controlled route. Review every spill and damage event at shift handover and close all open quarantine records before the next shift starts.

title: Incident Reporting
text:
1. Report every injury, near miss, vehicle contact, pedestrian conflict, spill, leak, fire alarm, evacuation, rack impact and equipment failure immediately to the shift supervisor on duty.
2. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
3. Notify the shift supervisor in person or by radio without leaving an unsafe condition unattended.
4. Stop the work involved, make the area safe, and preserve the scene for review.
5. Provide the time, exact location, persons involved, equipment involved, and a brief description of what happened.
6. Record the initial report in the designated incident log before the end of the shift in which the event occurred.
7. Attach scanner records, temperature records or load documents where relevant to support review.
8. Classify the report on submission as PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, or PR-14 Emergency evacuation where one applies.
9. Use PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for any contact between trucks, racking, doors, levellers, pallets or infrastructure, and for any seat-belt, brake, steering or lifting defect found in use.
10. Use PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse for any vehicle-pedestrian near miss, walkway, crossing or barrier defect, or breach of segregated routes.
11. Use PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any leak, spill, damaged hazmat container, vapour release or cage access issue, and keep the spill area guarded until the shift supervisor attends.
12. Use PR-14 Emergency evacuation for any alarm activation, evacuation, assembly-point issue, missing person report or refusal to evacuate.
13. Report incidents occurring on Shift 1, which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, to the Shift 1 supervisor before 14:00.
14. Report incidents occurring on Shift 2, which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, to the Shift 2 supervisor before 22:00.
15. Transfer any open incident that spans the shift change through the end-of-shift handover with the scene status, actions taken and attendance confirmed.
16. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report.
17. Complete the review on the same shift wherever possible, confirm classification, identify immediate cause, and order containment, segregation, quarantine or equipment isolation as required.
18. Interview witnesses separately, check the floor position, and record findings, corrective actions and the names of persons briefed.
19. Reassign duties, suspend the task or close the affected location until control measures are confirmed.
20. Escalate without delay to the warehouse manager where injury requires external treatment, evacuation was ordered, structural damage is suspected, or normal operation cannot safely resume.
21. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
22. Accept the shift supervisor review as the controlling operational decision until the warehouse manager directs otherwise.
23. Track each report to closure and confirm that corrective actions are implemented and briefed to affected staff.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Apply PR-14 Emergency evacuation to every evacuation of the building, without exception for shift, zone, or type of emergency.
2. Treat every alarm as a real evacuation order.
3. Stop all handling work immediately when the alarm sounds.
4. Lower truck forks, secure pallet jacks, and leave loads where they will not block main transport aisles or pedestrian routes.
5. Switch off MHE where it stands if it can be left safely.
6. Leave paperwork, scanners, and personal items in place.
7. Move by the nearest safe pedestrian route to the nearest safe exit.
8. Keep to the segregated walkways and marked crossings where they are available on the escape route.
9. Do not use forklifts, reach trucks, or electric pallet jacks to leave the building during evacuation.
10. Do not return to Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E, or Zone F to collect goods, equipment, or documents.
11. Close doors behind you where this does not delay escape.
12. Proceed directly to the designated assembly point.
13. Report to the shift supervisor at the assembly point on arrival.
14. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
15. Obey the shift supervisor's instructions at the assembly point.
16. Remain at the assembly point until formally released.
17. Do not leave the assembly point to move vehicles in the yard or to re-enter dock areas.
18. The shift supervisor will conduct roll call of all floor staff, visitors, and contractors present on that shift.
19. Report any missing person, last known location inside the building, and any known hazard to the shift supervisor without delay.
20. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
21. Liaise with the emergency services through the shift supervisor or the warehouse manager only.
22. Do not provide separate instructions to the emergency services from the assembly point.
23. Roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.
24. Do not re-enter the building after roll call until the authorised all-clear is given.
25. Re-enter only when directed, in the order directed, and return to the assigned work area.
26. Resume work only when instructed by the shift supervisor after re-entry.
27. Report any damage, blocked route, or unsafe condition found after re-entry immediately.
28. Maintain evacuation readiness on every shift.
29. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
30. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
31. Confirm on taking over the shift that all present staff know the escape routes, exits, and assembly point.
32. Brief all visitors on escape routes and the assembly point before they enter the floor.
33. An evacuation drill runs every quarter.
34. Attend the quarterly drill when on shift.
35. Treat the drill exactly as a real evacuation under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

title: Checks, Drills and Handover
text:
1. Carry out routine safety checks before operations start each day.
Document every check in the designated log and rectify defects before use. Notify the maintenance technician of any fault found on MHE, racking or dock equipment for logging and repair.

2. Execute PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation checks without exception.
Complete the documented pre-use check of every forklift each day. Perform the daily forklift check before first use each day and record the result before moving the truck.

3. Keep the maintenance technician responsible for follow-up on all equipment defects.
The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Isolate defective equipment from service until the maintenance technician clears it for return to use.

4. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift.
Record the reading in the shift record and escalate any deviation immediately. Suspend routine chilled work while a verified temperature excursion is under recovery.

5. Inspect racking under a documented monthly programme.
Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Report upright damage, beam deformation, missing safety pins or anchor failure at once and block the affected bay until cleared and released.

6. Practise PR-14 Emergency evacuation through a quarterly drill.
An evacuation drill runs every quarter. Time the evacuation, check roll-call discipline at the assembly point and log attendance and deficiencies for corrective action.

7. Hold the shift supervisor accountable for shift safety oversight.
The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direct all safety concerns, equipment faults and evacuation issues during the shift to that supervisor.

8. Submit every incident report for review within the same shift system.
The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Ensure reports are complete, legible and entered in the designated log before the end of the shift in which the event occurred.

9. Conduct PR-15 End-of-shift handover as a safety handover, not an administrative formality.
Walk the floor to confirm the state of equipment, racking, cold-zone condition, open incidents and quarantine positions. Brief the incoming team face to face on outstanding risks, stopped equipment and pending corrective actions.

10. Never leave safety ownership ambiguous between shifts.
Confirm that the incoming shift supervisor accepts the stated floor position before releasing duty. Carry forward unresolved variances, open incident actions and incomplete checks as explicit handover items for the next shift to close.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The role directs all activity across the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2, with 2,400 high-bay pallet positions and 8 dock doors.

1. Own site operations across PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, PR-06 Outbound dispatch, PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
2. Lead the direct reporting line for the shift, technical and inventory functions. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
3. Direct inbound, handling and value-added teams through their defined duties. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
4. Maintain operating hours across Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Enforce traffic and storage limits on every shift. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
6. Control racking, unit weight and outbound flow. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift.
7. Account for temperature-controlled and hazardous stock. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
8. Act as final sign-off for inventory assurance. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule.
9. Govern loss and exception decisions. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery.
10. Authorise safety-critical personnel and equipment use. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
11. Oversee rostering, dispatch coordination and incident governance. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. An evacuation drill runs every quarter.

title: Shift Supervisor
text:
1. Run one assigned shift with full responsibility for floor staff and incident response, directing all activity across Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E and Zone F during rostered hours.
2. Cover Shift 1 from 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 from 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, maintaining continuous supervision until formal handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
3. Supervise inbound operators who unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A, which is the receiving zone with inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection; dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
4. Coordinate with dispatchers, who book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, while the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers in Zone D, the dispatch zone with outbound staging in front of docks 5-8; dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
5. Direct forklift operators who operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks, enforcing that forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building, must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
6. Verify daily that every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day and that forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
7. Control picking through pickers who pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks, where Zone C is the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, in line with PR-04 Order picking.
8. Oversee put-away into Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, enforcing a maximum of 2,700 kg per rack bay, a maximum pallet weight of 800 kg including its load, free block-stacked pallets not above 4.0 m in height and not above 3 pallets high.
9. Maintain safe movement on 4.0 m wide main transport aisles, 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles and 1.2 m wide segregated pedestrian walkways, with high-visibility vests mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 mandatory on the warehouse floor, and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse applied throughout.
10. Support stock controllers who own inventory accuracy through cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, ensuring cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, with a second count completed before any stock adjustment is posted; only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.
11. Administer PR-09 Damaged-goods handling by approving damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and escalating damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR for warehouse-manager approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
12. Manage returns under PR-07 Returns handling and PR-01 Inbound receiving, confirming returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery, returns are inspected in Zone F, inspection occurs before any restock, rework or scrap decision, and returns staff proposals to restock, rework or scrap are decided by the shift supervisor, who approves the final disposition of inspected returns.
13. Supervise Zone E, the cold zone for chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, requiring the cold zone to stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.
14. Monitor Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, containing the quarantine area, returns inspection and the hazmat cage inside Zone F, where no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored at one time, equivalent to at most 5 full-weight pallets.
15. Lead response under PR-06 Outbound dispatch and PR-14 Emergency evacuation, reviewing every incident report, ensuring roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building, and ensuring an evacuation drill runs every quarter.

title: Dispatcher
text:
1. Book all inbound and outbound transport against confirmed orders and communicate arrival windows to carriers and the floor team.
2. Assign dock doors and time slots to every carrier, retaining sole authority for the schedule across both shifts.
3. Control the building with 8 dock doors, keeping Dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving and Dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch without exception.
4. Coordinate Zone A as the receiving zone for inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
5. Verify that the document check happens before unloading at receiving, and refuse early unloading where paperwork remains incomplete.
6. Manage Zone D as the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8 under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
7. Release each outbound load in the system before movement to the door, and withhold release where scans, counts or wrapping remain unresolved.
8. Plan trailer loads on a payload of 22000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions for contracted curtain-side trailers.
9. Limit every trailer to at most 27 full-weight pallets, since a pallet including its load may weigh at most 800 kg.
10. Deploy the delivery van for small consignments on a payload of 1200 kg and 6 pallet positions, loading at most 1 full-weight pallets and sending heavier orders by trailer.
11. Schedule the 4 outbound dock doors at 3 trailer loads per shift, protecting outbound capacity of at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift.
12. Balance bookings across Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, preventing queue overlap at shift change.
13. Record bookings, door allocations, releases and variances for PR-15 End-of-shift handover and brief the incoming dispatcher on open loads.
14. Wear high-visibility vest and safety footwear class S3 whenever present on the warehouse floor, and require the same from escorted drivers in operational areas.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. Unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A as the core duty of the role, covering inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
2. Staff the building with 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving, and operate each door only with its dock leveller, with one leveller fitted at each of the 8 dock doors.
3. Execute PR-01 Inbound receiving in strict sequence: complete the document check BEFORE unloading, carry out unloading BEFORE inspection, and complete inspection BEFORE booking goods into the system.
4. Book inspected goods into the system BEFORE any release for PR-02 Put-away to storage, and never stage unbooked pallets for transfer to Zone B.
5. Transfer system-booked ambient pallets toward Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, and keep put-away staging clear of main transport aisles 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways 1.2 m wide.
6. Reject any pallet including its load weighing more than 800 kg, any free block-stacked pallets exceeding 4.0 m in height or 3 pallets high, and any reserve instruction that would load a rack bay above 2,700 kg.
7. Direct chilled inbound goods under PR-12 Cold-chain handling to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +8 °C, and ensure the cold zone stays at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C with manual temperature verification each shift.
8. Segregate hazardous inbound items under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for movement only to the hazmat cage inside Zone F, noting Zone F holds the value-added services area and the quarantine area is in Zone F.
9. Maintain floor discipline for powered equipment around receiving: observe that forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building, must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
10. Wear mandatory personal protection at all times on the warehouse floor: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory.
11. Operate the allocated pallet-handling fleet safely in Zone A, drawn from 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks, and return equipment to defined staging after use.
12. Share 20 handheld WMS scanners with pickers for receipt verification, system booking and label checks, reporting faults promptly and returning units for charging.
13. Work rostered hours on either Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, including handover of open receipts, exceptions and staged loads.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. Core duty: forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks across receiving, storage, picking and dispatch.
2. Authorisation to operate is granted only by the warehouse manager; no operator may drive without that authorisation under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
3. Within Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, provide put-away to Zone B, replenishment to Zone C and loading support in Zone D as tasked.
4. Before first use each day complete the documented pre-use check for every forklift; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5. Operate the assigned fleet within rated limits: 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.
6. Observe site speed limits at all times: not exceed 8 km/h inside the building, not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
7. Under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse respect segregated infrastructure: main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide.
8. Wear mandatory personal protection on the warehouse floor: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, and forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
9. Execute PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system release: goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage; move system-booked pallets from Zone A, the receiving zone with inbound dock doors 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection, to Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking providing 2,400 pallet positions.
10. Respect storage limits on every move: each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, a pallet including its load may weigh at most 800 kg, free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high.
11. Execute PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces so that pick faces are replenished before the picking shift starts; deliver reserve stock to Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, and return afterwards to scheduled tasks.
12. Support Zone D, the dispatch zone with outbound staging in front of dock doors 5-8, where dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving, dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch and each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; note contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 22000 kg with 33 floor pallet positions, taking at most 27 full-weight pallets.
13. Handle temperature-controlled moves under PR-12 Cold-chain handling: Zone E is the cold zone for chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, which must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C.
14. Handle hazardous moves under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response: the hazmat cage is inside Zone F, covers 60 m2, holds no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time and holds at most 5 full-weight pallets, while Zone F holds the value-added services area.
15. Use shared resources as directed and leave them ready: pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, return scanners and equipment to designated positions at end of shift.

title: Pickers
text:
1. Pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks issued by the warehouse management system under PR-04 Order picking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Accept only system-directed tasks and complete them in the instructed sequence.
2. Work the assigned rostered shift in full floor personal protective equipment. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
3. Confirm pick-face availability at shift start before commencing PR-04 Order picking. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces from bulk reserve. Never pick from an empty, damaged or unreplenished location; report the shortfall immediately.
4. Collect one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners shared with inbound staff from the charging station and log on with personal identity. Return the scanner to charging at shift end. Report any shortage or fault without delay.
5. At each pick location scan the source location label first, then scan each picked item or carton as directed. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing. Reject any scan mismatch and leave the stock in place for investigation.
6. Use electric pallet jacks or hand pallet jacks for movement of picked goods within Zone C. The fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Operate only equipment for which training is held and park equipment clear of pick faces when not in use.
7. Observe all transport segregation while moving through shared areas. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Remain inside the walkways on foot and cross only at marked crossings.
8. Give way to mechanised handling equipment at all interfaces. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Make eye contact with the driver before stepping out and never assume priority.
9. Maintain pick-face discipline during the shift. Keep cartons correctly faced, labels visible and flow-rack lanes clear. Remove stretch film, strapping and empty cartons to waste cages. Never stage excess stock in picking aisles.
10. Perform PR-05 Packing and labelling only after successful scan verification. Confirm quantities, item identity and carton condition against the scanner task before sealing, labelling or consolidating. Segregate any damaged, short or mislabelled unit and notify supervision.
11. Respect handling limits for every unit built. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Distribute weight evenly, keep loads stable and within the pallet footprint, and request rework of any unstable or overweight unit.
12. Transfer completed packed units to Zone D as directed by the system. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Place units only in the assigned staging lane and never substitute between lanes. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for outbound pallets where the task requires wrapping.
13. Coordinate replenishment needs without leaving Zone C unattended. Reserve stock for replenishment is drawn from Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Flag urgent shorts to supervision for priority top-up under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces and continue with the next system task.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. Own inventory accuracy across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Coordinate all count activity under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts and maintain auditable system records for every location.

2. Execute cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Cover Zone B bulk storage with high-bay pallet racking, Zone C picking with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, Zone E cold storage, and the quarantine area in Zone F.

3. Operate across Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, to sustain count coverage. Collect handheld WMS scanners from the designated point; pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, so confirm availability at shift start.

4. Apply disciplined scanning and entry on every count. Scan each location and item as directed and post a second count before any stock adjustment is posted. Never post an adjustment on a first count alone.

5. Lead the full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year. Freeze movements as instructed, direct count teams by zone, reconcile variances, and submit results for sign-off. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.

6. Verify storage compliance while counting the 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay racking. Confirm each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, each pallet including its load weighs at most 800 kg, and free block-stacked pallets do not exceed 4.0 m in height or 3 pallets high. Segregate and report any non-conformance found.

7. Support safe movement through the count zones. Work within main transport aisles 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles 3.0 m wide, keeping equipment and totes clear of travel paths. Wear high-visibility vests and safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor at all times.

8. Perform cold-chain verification each shift in Zone E under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Check that the cold zone, chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, stays at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, record the reading as instructed, and escalate any excursion without delay.

9. Process damage findings under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Initiate recounts, preserve evidence, and route write-offs to the correct approver: the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, while damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

10. Assist the documented racking safety inspection every month by providing count data, confirming bay loads, and reporting beam or upright defects for technical review. Keep all count, recount, adjustment and temperature records complete and available for audit.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. Inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for every unit received under PR-07 Returns handling.
2. Accept returns only within 14 days of delivery and verify eligibility against the system record before moving goods inward.
3. Complete inspection in Zone F before any restock, rework or scrap decision is requested.
4. Submit each proposed disposition to the shift supervisor and proceed only after approval of the final disposition.
5. Transfer approved rework units to the designated holding position inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
6. Carry out packing, labelling, kitting and packing rework in line with PR-05 Packing and labelling.
7. Scan-verify picked items before packing and confirm label data against the outbound load record.
8. Operate within Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, as rostered.
9. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor.
10. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor.
11. Use handheld WMS scanners from the shared pool of 20 units for all returns, packing and labelling transactions.
12. Move low-level units with the site pool of 12 hand pallet jacks and keep pedestrian routes clear.
13. Feed outbound pallets through the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in dispatch and prepare waste for the 1 cardboard baler.
14. Stage packed and wrapped pallets for Zone D, which is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
15. Segregate any unit showing damage and complete PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment before further use or adjustment.
16. Route write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval and write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval.
17. Handle chilled returns under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and protect the cold zone, which is chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
18. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C during all inspection and packing tasks.
19. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to any hazardous return and store approved hazmat only in the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
20. Respect that the hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and that no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
21. Plan cage placements on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets, calculated from the stock limit and maximum pallet weight.
22. Observe that a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg when building, moving or proposing restock units.
23. Keep free block-stacked pallets within 4.0 m in height and within 3 pallets high where block stacking is directed.
24. Move pallets found outside the permitted temperature range and other quarantined stock to the quarantine area, which is in Zone F, and hold them for assessment.
Returns and Packing Staff work permanently between inspection, value-added work and quarantine control. Returns are inspected in Zone F, rework and labelling are executed there, and quarantine holds are managed there until authorised release.
Coordination with inbound, stock control and dispatch keeps restock, scrap and outbound packing aligned to system tasks and supervisor approvals.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. Maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment across the site and log all repairs. Provide cover across Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, as rostered.
2. Own the fleet under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation: 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. Verify that the daily forklift check happens before first use each day.
3. Ensure every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. Review submitted check sheets, quarantine defective trucks, and authorise return to service only after repair and logging.
4. Maintain 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, 1 cardboard baler, and 8 dock doors where each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Keep repair logs current for all defects, parts used and release dates.
5. Inspect high-bay pallet racking in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking. Cover the full warehouse floor of 6,000 m2 where the high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions.
6. Complete a documented safety inspection of racking every month. Enforce that each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, and block any overloaded bay from further use until rectified.
7. Support safe movement standards across the layout. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
8. Maintain segregation infrastructure to defined widths: main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Act on reported defects under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
9. Wear mandatory personal protection on the warehouse floor at all times. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, and forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
10. Support PR-12 Cold-chain handling in the cold zone: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift. Maintain refrigeration plant, doors, seals and monitoring devices to sustain that range.
11. Support PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for the hazmat cage inside Zone F, which covers 60 m2. Ensure no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, equivalent to at most 5 full-weight pallets. Maintain containment, ventilation, signage and spill equipment and log all interventions.
12. Support the quarantine area in Zone F through repair of barriers, signage and lighting, ensuring quarantined stock remains segregated and identifiable.
13. Support PR-14 Emergency evacuation and the quarterly evacuation drill programme. Secure plant and isolate energy sources as directed, noting that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

title: Inbound Receiving Hours and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. receives inbound goods in Zone A, the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection at inbound docks 1-4.
2. The building provides 8 dock doors in total, with dock doors 1-4 dedicated to inbound receiving.
3. Receiving operates across two shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. Within those hours inbound intake is executed under PR-01 Inbound receiving, followed by PR-02 Put-away to storage.
5. All carrier arrivals require a pre-booked slot.
6. The dispatcher books transport and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
7. Upon arrival at the assigned door, inbound operators complete the document check before unloading.
8. Assigned inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
9. Every delivery is inspected before it is booked into the system.
10. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners for system booking and verification tasks.
11. Goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage.
12. Put-away from Zone A is system-directed and completed under PR-02 Put-away to storage.
13. Dispatchers also assign dock doors for outbound and release outbound loads, keeping inbound doors 1-4 clear for the receiving programme.
14. Harborwick commits to process booked inbound vehicles received within the published receiving hours through document check, unloading, inspection and system booking on the day of arrival.
15. Where inspection identifies shortage, damage or documentation mismatch, the goods are held from booking pending resolution under the intake standard, and the carrier is notified of the exception.
16. Intake performance is measured against slot adherence, time from arrival to system booking, and inspection accuracy, and is reported to the client on the agreed service schedule.

title: Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. undertakes outbound dispatch from Zone D, which provides outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Across the building Harborwick operates 8 dock doors, with dock doors 5-8 dedicated to outbound dispatch.

3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for loading under this agreement.

4. Dispatch operates across two shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

5. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads for both shifts.

6. For every outbound movement the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and carriers are loaded only against that assigned door and slot.

7. All orders are prepared under PR-05 Packing and labelling before handover to PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging and loading.

8. To protect load integrity dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for outbound pallets.

9. For safe vehicle interfacing each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller, including all outbound doors.

10. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound loads carry a payload of 22000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions.

11. Because a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, a trailer takes at most 27 full-weight pallets.

12. Our delivery van used for small consignments carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions.

13. On that basis the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

14. Within these equipment limits each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.

15. Accordingly outbound capacity is at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.

16. Lighter pallets may use more of the available floor positions up to the stated trailer and van limits, subject to weight, stability and dispatcher confirmation.

17. A staging lane is released for loading only after the dispatcher has released that outbound load in the system.

18. Loads not released by the dispatcher-confirmed cut-off time for the booked slot will be rebooked to the next available door and slot, with the client notified of the revised departure.

title: Order Accuracy and Pick-Pack Standard
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. maintains pick-face availability as the foundation of order accuracy under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces and PR-04 Order picking. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
2. Replenished faces will be available at shift start for all scheduled order waves. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts. Replenishment shortfalls affecting wave start will be notified to the client record with location, quantity short, and revised availability time.
3. Bulk reserve stock supporting accuracy remains system-directed from high-bay racking to ground-level faces. Under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, Harbourwick commits to complete scheduled top-ups before release of picking tasks, preserving location integrity between reserve and pick face.
4. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. PR-04 Order picking will be executed only against live system tasks on handheld devices. Paper-based substitute picking will not be used to confirm accuracy where system tasks are available.
5. Scanning discipline underpins every picked unit. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, allocated to preserve picking continuity during inbound peaks. Each pick will be verified by scanning at the pick face in line with system prompts before tote transfer.
6. Verified packing forms the contractual accuracy control under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing. Any item failing scan verification will be held from the pack, re-checked against the order task, and corrected before sealing.
7. Packed consignments will carry correct principal labelling matched to the outbound order before transfer to outbound staging. Packing checks will confirm item quantity, variant, and destination label agreement. Mismatched or unscanned units will not proceed to Zone D staging.
8. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Completed, scan-verified packs will be staged in Zone D for loading only after system recording. Harbourwick commits to release staged loads against confirmed transport bookings, maintaining traceability from pick face to dispatch staging.

title: Storage Zones and Capacity Limits
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. stores client inventory across a 6,000 m2 warehouse floor under controlled put-away and location management.
2. Bulk reserve stock is held in Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, providing 2,400 pallet positions for client goods.
3. Active order fulfilment stock is held in Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, fed from Zone B reserve locations.
4. Under PR-02 Put-away to storage, every inbound pallet is booked into the system before physical put-away to its storage location.
5. Without completed system booking, no pallet will be directed to Zone B racking or Zone C pick faces, ensuring full traceability from receipt to storage.
6. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg anywhere in the warehouse, including racking, pick faces and block-stacked areas.
7. Pallets exceeding that gross weight will not be accepted into storage locations and will be held for reassessment and client instruction.
8. Each rack bay in Zone B may carry at most 2,700 kg in total across its beam levels.
