9. Distribution of weight within the bay respects system direction and bay rating, protecting rack integrity and product safety.
10. Where racking locations are unavailable and the system explicitly directs block stacking, free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
11. In the same block-stacked configuration, free stacks must not exceed 4.0 m in height, applying whichever limit is reached first.
12. Harborwick commits to monitor bay loads and stack heights during put-away, replenishment and cycle counting, correcting any excess without delay.
13. Client reporting reflects system-booked locations only, so stored quantities in Zone B and Zone C always align with PR-02 Put-away to storage records.
14. Capacity allocation across the 2,400 pallet positions is managed to preserve access, rotation and safety, with bulk and picking balances reviewed on each working day.

title: Cycle Counts and Annual Stocktake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. performs all inventory verification under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts as the binding site standard.
2. Under that procedure, stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments across every storage location.
3. For daily assurance, cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule without exception for operational pressure.
4. Within each cycle count, locations are counted, variances are isolated, and a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
5. No adjustment arising from a cycle count will be posted on a first count alone, and every adjustment retains its supporting counts for audit.
6. Beyond daily counting, a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year covering all stock on site at that date.
7. During the annual event, movements in the counted areas are frozen under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts until controlled release.
8. Following completion of counting, all variances are recounted, since a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
9. Only once recounts are complete will proposed adjustments be compiled for review with full count evidence attached.
10. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results, and no annual result is reported to the client without that sign-off.
11. Reflecting wider accountability, the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
12. That accountability includes approval of the annual stocktake plan, resourcing of counting teams, and final acceptance of adjustments.
13. After sign-off, the approved adjustments are posted promptly and the client receives a reconciliation of opening position, counts, adjustments and closing position.
14. Throughout the year, the client receives cycle-count performance within the agreed stock report, including locations counted, hit rate and open variances.
15. Where a variance remains unresolved after recount, it is carried forward under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts rather than forced to zero.
16. In this way, daily discipline and annual completeness combine to sustain accurate inventory for fulfilment and billing.

title: Stock Reporting and Accountability
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. maintains a single system inventory as the binding stock record for all client holdings. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.

2. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. The client receives a cycle-count report for each working day, confirming locations counted, system quantities and variances carried forward for recount.

3. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.

4. Following annual sign-off, Harborwick issues a formal stocktake reconciliation within the agreed reporting window. That reconciliation states the approved opening position, the counted quantities, the posted adjustments and the closing system position.

5. No stock adjustment arising from PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts is reported as final until the required second count and stock-controller review are complete. Harborwick reports open variances as provisional and confirms the final adjusted figure once approved.

6. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report, including any incident affecting stock integrity, packaging or handling equipment, before the record is included in client reporting.

7. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and only released outbound loads are deducted from the reported closing stock for the shift.

8. To preserve reporting integrity around movements, Harborwick applies a daily cut-off tied to dispatch release and system booking. Movements after cut-off appear in the next working day report with their system timestamps.

9. As supporting assurance, racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Where an inspection restricts a bay, Harborwick reports the affected locations and confirms any relocated stock by system location.

10. Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift. The shift record supports the chilled-stock report, and any verified deviation suspends routine chilled reporting until recovery readings confirm the compliant condition.

11. Harborwick retains all count sheets, recount records, adjustment approvals, stocktake sign-off and incident reviews for audit. The warehouse manager provides final sign-off on escalated accuracy exceptions and annual results.

12. Client queries on any report receive a documented response with the underlying system evidence. Agreed corrections are posted as formal adjustments with reason codes and reflected in the next scheduled report.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. segregates all damaged, suspect and non-conforming stock on the day of discovery and holds it exclusively in the quarantine area in Zone F pending assessment and disposition.

2. Inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, quarantine stock remains physically separated from saleable inventory, from value-added work and from all other Zone F holdings until formally released through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

3. Upon identification, floor staff transfer the affected pallet, carton or unit to quarantine without further put-away, picking or dispatch, while system records retain the original location, quantity and reason for holding until assessment is complete.

4. Assessment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling determines restock, rework or scrap for each quarantine line, with photographic evidence, quantity, value and cause retained against the client stock record.

5. For financial control, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. applies a write-off threshold of 500 EUR per damage event as a firm client commitment.

6. Within that control, the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.

7. Above that threshold, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and only the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, may authorise the higher-value adjustment.

8. To support transparency, the shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising from damage events, including cause, handling and corrective action, and quarantine status forms part of daily operational reporting.

9. No quarantined goods return to saleable stock, transfer to rework or leave the site as scrap without documented PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment and the applicable write-off approval under items 6 and 7.

10. At month end, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. reconciles all quarantine holdings in Zone F against incident reports and write-off approvals, ensuring open quarantine lines, approved disposals and pending decisions are fully visible in client reporting.

11. Through this quarantine discipline, prompt same-day segregation and tiered financial approval, clients receive assured protection of inventory integrity, clear accountability for loss and consistent application of PR-09 Damaged-goods handling across all shifts.

title: Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick commits to accept authorised returns within 14 days of delivery, subject to customer reference and delivery verification against the system record.

Requests received after that acceptance window will be declined, unless the client has agreed an exception in writing before the goods are returned to site. Unauthorised arrivals without prior agreement will be held pending instruction and will not enter inspection.

2. All returns handling will be performed under PR-07 Returns handling as the controlling procedure for receipt, inspection and disposition.

Under PR-07 Returns handling no restock, rework or scrap decision will be made until inspection has been completed and recorded. Inspection will always precede any restock, rework or scrap decision.

3. Harborwick will direct every authorised return to Zone F for inspection and assessment.

Zone F holds the value-added services area, providing segregated space away from bulk storage and picking for controlled examination of returned goods. Returns are inspected in Zone F and no inspection will take place in receiving, storage or dispatch zones.

4. Dedicated returns staff will inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each line.

Each proposal will identify quantity, condition and reason for the recommendation, with supporting system notes to allow approval. Segregation will be maintained between awaiting-inspection, approved and rejected units until disposition is confirmed.

5. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, including authority over returns disposition on that shift.

Harborwick assigns disposition control to the on-duty leadership so decisions are taken promptly during operating hours. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns and no restock, rework or scrap action will proceed without that prior approval.

6. Upon disposition approval Harborwick commits to execute the agreed outcome without delay.

Approved restock units will be returned to saleable inventory through system-directed put-away. Approved rework units will transfer to value-added processing, while approved scrap units will be removed from inventory and held for authorised disposal.

7. Harborwick will maintain a complete audit record for every return from arrival through final disposition.

For each case the record will show acceptance against the 14-day rule, Zone F inspection findings, the returns staff proposal and the shift supervisor approval. Disposition actions will be traceable to PR-07 Returns handling for client review.

title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides chilled storage in Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.

2. All client stock requiring controlled refrigeration under PR-12 Cold-chain handling will be held only in Zone E.

3. We commit to maintain Zone E at or above +2 °C at all times during storage and handling.

4. Equally, Zone E will be maintained at or below +8 °C at all times during storage and handling.

5. Continuous monitoring operates in Zone E with automated alerting for excursion risk.

6. Beyond automated monitoring, cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift using calibrated devices.

7. Each manual verification is recorded with reading, device and time, and retained against PR-12 Cold-chain handling records.

8. Assigned floor staff perform the per-shift verification at the defined monitoring points in Zone E.

9. During each shift, the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, including ownership of the cold-chain response.

10. Where any manual check or automated alert indicates a deviation from +2 to +8 °C, the shift supervisor initiates the PR-12 Cold-chain handling excursion response without delay.

11. Affected pallets are segregated and assessed before any further storage, replenishment or picking decision.

12. Clients receive prompt notification of any verified excursion affecting their stock, including duration, product scope and corrective action.

13. Normal chilled operations resume only after restoration of the committed range is confirmed.

14. Overall accountability rests with site leadership, as the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

15. Under that accountability, Harborwick maintains calibration of monitoring devices, training of Zone E personnel, and availability of backup controls to protect continuity of the +2 to +8 °C condition.

16. Cold-chain performance, including per-shift verification compliance and any excursions, forms part of routine client reporting under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

17. For audit purposes, temperature records for Zone E are retained and made available to the client on request, demonstrating continuous compliance with the at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C commitments.
